title: Counting crossings from still photographs
learning_goal: Understand Rice's formula as 'a toll counter without a clock' and see it reproduce the true crossing rate from snapshots plus the equations.
takeaway: A shoebox of snapshots plus the equations gives the crossing rate without running time forward.
notes: All scenes are ready (D4): no simulation, training or benchmark; every number comes from E1 results already in the repository. The T4 chapter card sits in the 3.2-s lead-in of 05.1 (tier 0 lit, rail stays at L2; the climb to L3 is in 05.5, which is also the checkpoint). Predict beat: one unnumbered beat in 05.1 ('Can one photo, with no time in it, give you a rate?', hold 2.5 s, reads PREDICT on screen): the outline had none in ch05 and the misconception it targets (a rate needs a clock) is the chapter's whole point. Changes against the outline, to review: (1) 05.2 reopens the 04.6 shoebox at Gamma = 0.93 (outline: 0.9) so the box is the same object; it reads data/e1_samples_0.93.json plus a NEW small file data/ch05_rice.json, block strip (26 of the 8,000 snapshots fall in |D| < 0.2; 21 at 0.9). The sparse strip is shown and said, not hidden (critique C13), and it motivates 05.5 ('plenty of snapshots'); no re-integration (D4) and no Rice value of this single box is quoted. (2) 05.3 reads data/e1_finegrid.json plus the same NEW file data/ch05_rice.json, block check, with the two cumulative errors (recomputed from e1_gissinger.json grille_fine: 0.0437 and 0.0593, i.e. the report's 4% and 6%), so that no percentage is typed in a scene; the cumulative error is defined visually as shaded area / area under the counted curve (critique C7), a device 09.1 reuses. (3) The core cut loses the 'three-variable deterministic system' caveat to X4.1, so 05.3 keeps it audible in one sentence ('on three chaotic dials where the formula's fine print is not even guaranteed', R:883, R:901). (4) 05.4 adds one sentence on counting crossings of a level farther from zero (T:680), which sets up the question card; the excursion is said to add two crossings, consistent with 04.3. Badges: SCHEMATIC for the toll counter (a thought experiment with no numbers; if the lead keeps only the five BRIEF kinds, use PROVED with note 'counting formula, R:520'), PROVED for 05.2 (Proposition 8) and 05.4 (what the formula counts, R:528; T Prop. 2.30), MEASURED for 05.3 (E1), none on the bridge 05.5 and on the question card. No external fact: Kac 1943 and Rice 1944-1945 are in the report's bibliography (R:1508-1511), so no web source is needed. Symbol sheet: r_0 for the crossing rate (never nu_0), r and r_a only on the formula layer of 05.4, Gissinger coefficient as the number 0.1, 'crossing rate' on screen, 'cumulative error' never 'within'. Question card numbered n = 6 on the assumption of one card per chapter in order (ch04.Q = 5): the consistency editor may renumber. Words budgeted at 125-130 effective words per minute against target_s (minus the predict hold and the chapter-card lead-in in 05.1); estimates use the assembler formula (146 raw words per minute, 0.9 s per paragraph break, holds, lead-in and tail). Data note for the foundation engineer: data/e1_finegrid.json labels its 'bridge' block 'P(|D| < h)' with h_rice 0.2, but the stored bridge masses are P(|D| < 0.25) (experiences/e1_gissinger.py pont_* use 0.25; R:729, R:807): ch05 does not use them, 09.x and 07.x might. scenes.title: A toll counter without a clock

predict.title: PREDICT
predict.question: One photo, no clock: can it give a rate?

sentences.text: A puzzle. How many cars cross this line each hour?
No clock. Just one photo from above, where every speedometer can be read.
Can one photo, with no time in it, give you a rate?
It can. Draw a thin strip around the line.
A fast car spends little time inside, so catching one there counts for more.
Add up the speeds of the cars inside, and divide by the strip's width.
On average, that is how many cars cross per hour.

onscreen.title: Counting crossings from still photographs
labels: One photo, no clock: can it give a rate?

scenes.title: Rice for the dipole

sentences.text: Back to the shoebox. Spread its photos out by their {b}dipole{/} reading.
The line to cross is zero: draw a thin strip around it.
Each photo also needs a speedometer.
No clock required: the dipole's equation turns the photo's three dial readings into a speed.
Up or down, both count, so keep only its size.
Add the speeds inside the strip, then divide by its width and by the total number of photos.
Out comes the {metric}crossing rate{/}.
Shrink the strip to nothing, and for well-behaved systems the recipe is exact: Rice's formula.
The catch: few photos land in a thin strip. Here, about two dozen out of eight thousand.

labels: sum of speeds in the strip ÷ strip width ÷ total number of photos

formulas.tex: \ck{r_0} = \int |y|\,p_{D,\dot D}(0,y)\,dy = \lim_{h\to 0}\tfrac{1}{2h}\,\mathbb{E}\big[|\dot D|\,\mathbf{1}_{|D|<h}\big]\ \ \text{if } D \text{ is stationary, } C^1, \text{ and } (D,\dot D) \text{ has a continuous density}
\hat r_0 = \tfrac{1}{N}\textstyle\sum_{i=1}^{N} |\dot D_i|\,\mathbf{1}_{|D_i|<h}/(2h),\ \ \dot D_i = -0.1\,D_i + V_i Q_i,\ \ h = 0.2;\ \ \text{bias } O(h^2),\ \text{variance } O(1/(Nh))

scenes.title: Check against the truth

sentences.text: Now test it against the truth.
At forty-one settings of {param}Gamma{/}, long simulations count the crossings as they happen.
Rice gets only the true snapshots, shuffled, plus the equations.
The two curves almost coincide.
Shade the gap, and divide by the area under the counted curve: the {metric}cumulative error{/}.
Four percent near the threshold, six percent above it.
A good sign, on three chaotic dials that are not even guaranteed to be well-behaved.

labels: cumulative error = shaded area ÷ area under the counted curve
say how often the field flips
chips: DATA · E1 · fine grid, 41 Γ (source lower-third from data/e1_finegrid.json meta)
three chaotic dials · strip width fixed at h = 0.2

scenes.title: Crossings are not reversals

sentences.text: One caution: Rice counts crossings, not reversals.
An excursion across zero and back adds two crossings, but no reversal.
To isolate reversals, the PhD plan counts crossings of a far level, on the other side.

question.en: For VKS, which *dipole* should Rice count, and what threshold turns a crossing into a *reversal*?
question.say: For VKS, which dipole should Rice count, and what threshold turns a crossing into a reversal?
question.fr: Pour VKS, quel dipôle la formule de Rice doit-elle suivre, et quel seuil fait d'un passage par zéro un renversement ?
question.why: The plan names two candidate dipoles; Rice needs u and B on each snapshot for the dipole's rate of change, and counts excursions too, while the plan leaves the threshold open.
question.unblocks: Which dipole series and which snapshot fields, u and B together, to request with the VKS simulation data, and the thresholds of tier 3's criterion (d).
question.why_fr: Le plan propose deux dipôles ; Rice a besoin de u et B sur chaque instantané pour la dérivée du dipôle, et compte aussi les excursions, alors que le plan laisse le seuil ouvert.
question.unblocks_fr: La série du dipôle et les champs, u et B ensemble, à demander avec les données de simulation VKS, et les seuils du critère (d) du palier 3.
